what_it_does: Designing a new processor requires predicting how fast it will run real programs — ideally before building any hardware. Cycle-accurate simulation (a software model that emulates every clock tick) is very accurate but painfully slow. Pure machine-learning models are fast but often wrong on unfamiliar designs. Concorde blends both: it uses physics-like equations derived from first principles (how pipelines, caches, and branch predictors behave) to capture the bulk of the performance, then uses a learned model to correct the leftover error from complex interactions the equations miss. Because the equations for each processor stage are written independently and composed together, the system can quickly evaluate many different design configurations.
